newsitem.title: FIJI: Striking Fiji sugar workers appeal to High Court.
newsitem.headline: Striking Fiji sugar workers appeal to High Court.

text.p: Fiji's striking sugar industry unionists filed an appeal in the Suva High Court on Tuesday against a Sugar Industry Tribunal order that they return to work.
The appeal was filed by the Fiji Sugar and General Workers Union. No date has been set for the hearing yet.
Industry sources said the parties in the sugar industry strike were requested on Tuesday to appear before arbitrators on Wednesday afternoon.

Fiji Sugar Corp (FSC) managing director Jonatani Galuinadi said in a statement on Tuesday that a speedy return to work by striking unionists could minimise loss and damage sustained by the sugar industry and Fiji's national economy.
The strike by about 2,000 workers on Tuesday entered its second week. It has been called over occupational health and safety concerns at the FSC's four sugar mills.
Before the strike, Fiji's 1997 raw sugar production was forecast at 440,000 tonnes, down from 475,000 tonnes in 1996.
The crush had been running well before the strike but FSC exports had already been affected by the strike, Sugar Tribunal acting chief Cyril Don Aidney said late last week.
